> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4f81f315266354e7b70adc589d6ee38a76d24f41` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea35a797847a3417588e5c51c9670ae845c6d176` — the merge of head `339604baf420a246fc5841dffd75d8a440346648` into base `4f81f315266354e7b70adc589d6ee38a76d24f41`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea35a797847a3417588e5c51c9670ae845c6d176 && git checkout ea35a797847a3417588e5c51c9670ae845c6d176
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4f81f315266354e7b70adc589d6ee38a76d24f41 339604baf420a246fc5841dffd75d8a440346648 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4f81f315266354e7b70adc589d6ee38a76d24f41 && git merge --no-ff 339604baf420a246fc5841dffd75d8a440346648

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4f81f315266354e7b70adc589d6ee38a76d24f41
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4f81f315266354e7b70adc589d6ee38a76d24f41` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `339604baf420a246fc5841dffd75d8a440346648`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23332 (body, triage first grade `6154972534`, the unlock scan, the PM claim, the os-dev-report), PR #23425 (body, 10-file list, net diff against `main` at the head; merge base `5656c5638`), and the check-runs on the head, read once. Reference reads of `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`, `component.zod.ts`, `migrations/entries/README.md` and ADR-0087 at the container's checkout (`e4ec6ec1a`, the claim's own read sha, pre-PR) to confirm what the diff builds on; nothing built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head.** Completed and green: `filter`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Spec property liveness`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check Changeset`, `Auto Label`. Skipped (opt-in or matrix placeholders): `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (${{ matrix.shard }}/3)`, `Console Pin Gate`. **In progress at brief time (18):** `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Test Core (1/6)` … `(6/6)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace`. Their conclusions are the derived-gate verdicts for the pins, the docs regeneration and the migration-registry entry; this record does not pre-empt them, and the branch protection (`mergeable_state: blocked`) holds the merge until they report.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **The four page action rows' `operation`: `z.unknown()` → `ActionSchema`'s own enum, by reference** (`component.zod.ts`, `actionOperation() = ActionSchema.in.shape.operation.unwrap()`, applied on `ActionButtonPropsSchema`, `ActionIconPropsSchema` and `actionContainerMemberShape()` for the `action:group` / `action:menu` members). Accept-set narrowing: any value but `'update'` is now refused at `operation`; `'delete'` / `'custom'` carry the enum's own error map ("bulk-def operation with no row-level form"), every other value `invalid_value`. **Right.** It is the triage direction verbatim ("the rows declare `operation` and judge it as `ActionSchema` does. One rule, read from one place, not a second copy"), the same read-by-reference pattern the rows already use for `onSuccess` (`actionOnSuccessBlock()`), and the NO SECOND VOCABULARY pin asserts identity of the enum instance on all four rows. The runner's `isUpdateOperationAction` tests `operation === 'update'`, so no previously-parsing non-`'update'` value did anything at run time.

2. **The rows refuse `onSuccess` beside `operation: 'update'` whatever executor the row names, ONE issue at `onSuccess`** (`refuseRowOnSuccessBesideExecutor` reads `operation` before `effectiveRowExecutor`). Accept-set narrowing for rows with `api` / `script` / a host handler plus the pairing; for the no-executor row it is a text change only (that row was already refused, with the no-executor text). **Right.** The card's "Wanted" bullet 1 (one answer in both places) and bullet 2 (the refusal text for an `operation: 'update'` row says what it does at run time) are both met, and the order of reads matches the runner's (`ActionRunner.ts:1384-1388` at the pin), so the no-executor case gets the fitting text, which was the card's named wording point. Pins on all four rows × {none, `api`, `script`, `run`}, each with a same-row negative control (no `onSuccess` parses), plus the `os validate` door pins in `packages/lint`.

3. **`ActionSchema`'s `DECLARATIVE_UPDATE_REFUSED_KEYS` `onSuccess` entry: text replaced, reach unchanged.** The entry stays keyed `onSuccess` in the same table, so the action accept set is identical before and after; only the message changes (from "`onSuccess` is not defined for an `operation: 'update'` action yet …" to the shared `onSuccessBesideUpdateOperationRefusal("An `operation: 'update'` action's `onSuccess`")`). **Right**, and the direction's "measurement moves the rule on ActionSchema's side" branch was not taken: the PR's premise check (runner docblock scopes `onSuccess` to `api`/`script`; objectui's `ActionDefaultInspector` `UPDATE_OPERATION_REFUSES` lists and clears it; no objectui test pins the pairing) is the measurement triage asked for, and it lands on `ActionSchema`'s refusal being the right half. ⛔ `ActionSchema` was not widened. Pin sweep: the one pin on the old text (`action-row-update.test.ts:218`) is flipped; the new `ActionSchema`-side test asserts ONE issue at `onSuccess` for `{}` and `{ type: 'script' }` with a negative control.

4. **One text from one place:** `onSuccessBesideUpdateOperationRefusal(subject)` added to `action-on-success-executor.ts` (the module PR #23331 created) and read by both `action.zod.ts` and `component.zod.ts`. **Right.** The module is not re-exported from `packages/spec/src/ui/index.ts` or `packages/spec/src/index.ts` (checked at the reference checkout), so this is an internal export, not a public-surface widening; the ONE TEXT pin compares the row message after its subject to `ActionSchema`'s after its subject, and the ablation table in the PR (row branch off → 20 red; action entry deleted → 6 red; enum back to `z.unknown()` → 9 red) shows each pin bears load.

5. **D3 semantic entry `18.ui-page-action-row-operation-declared.ts`**, id matching the changeset's `adr-0087: registered ui-page-action-row-operation-declared` marker, beside its `18.ui-page-action-row-*` family, in the per-file registry shape `entries/README.md` prescribes (no index to edit; `gen:migration-registry` concatenates). **Right.** `surface` names both narrowed keys on all four rows, `replacement` is marked NOT mechanically convertible (the author chooses between the write and the hop), `acceptanceCriteria` is non-empty and names the `os validate` finding paths.

6. **Generated docs** `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx`: 8 lines, the four rows' `operation` type cell (`any` → the enum of `'update'`) and `onSuccess` description (adds "and beside `operation: 'update'`, whose write the runner performs before any executor"). **Right** — matches the `.describe()` strings in the diff one for one; `Flag docs affected by code changes` is green and `Build Docs` is in progress.

7. **Unknown-members ledger** `component-props-unknown-members.pin.test.ts`: `operation` removed from `ACTION_RUNNER_PATHS`. **Right** — a typed member deletes its ledger line, as `onSuccess` did under PR #23331; the comment is updated to say so.

8. **Producers:** none in this repository (examples, CLI corpus, dogfood fixtures per the PR); objectui at pin `1fb1ced36243` and main `b9814b3` carries `operation: 'update'` rows without `onSuccess` (still accepted) and objectui's registration already publishes `operation` as `enum: ['update']`. hotcrm NOT MEASURED — carried to ③.

Nothing in the diff touches `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts` (#23357's surface) — the claim's exclusion holds.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/23332-page-action-row-operation.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM → TO table, ADR-0087 `registered` disposition naming the D3 entry, measured producers stated. **Matches what the diff publishes.** The only package whose published accept set changes is `@objectstack/spec` (`packages/lint` gains test-only lines; `content/docs` is generated). `minor` for a pre-GA metadata-facing accept-set narrowing is ADR-0087's stated level (the 2026-09-13 #18003 amendment: "Pre-GA, a metadata-facing retirement or break ships `minor`, carrying the `**BREAKING**` banner and its ADR-0087 disposition entry"), and it is the level the sibling narrowings `.changeset/23015-*`, `23072-*`, `15953-*` carry. `Check Changeset` is green.

Clause-②: the PM claim declared `yes` conditionally (a possible widening of `ActionSchema`); the PR, the changeset and the dev report declare `no (narrowing)`. **The diff is a narrowing on every surface it touches and widens none**: the rows refuse strictly more (items 1 and 2 above), `ActionSchema`'s accept set is byte-for-byte the same table of refused keys with one message reworded (item 3), and the new helper is not on the barrel (item 4). The widening the claim hedged against did not occur, and triage's own first-grade note records exactly this outcome as "Clause ②: `no` if the rows take the refusal". **Clause-②: no (narrowing) is right**, and the PR body's acceptance note explains the deviation from the claim, as required. (The sibling changeset #23015 spells the same class `yes (narrowing)`; the spelling convention is not this card's to settle — the direction of record for this card says `no`, and this review was rendered at contract tier regardless.)

Cosmetic, not a gate: the PR title is `fix(spec)!:` while the changeset heading is `feat(spec)!:`. Both carry `!`; the changeset is what versions.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: `[]` — none to answer.

Dev flags (`deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings` in the os-dev-report, and the PR's acceptance notes), each answered or escalated:

1. **Clause-② `yes` (claim) vs `no (narrowing)` (PR).** Answered in ②: the PR is right; the claim's `yes` was declared for a branch measurement ruled out.

2. **File surface: two test files outside the claim's listed surface** — `packages/spec/src/ui/component-props-unknown-members.pin.test.ts` and `packages/lint/src/validate-component-props-row-on-success.test.ts`. Answered: accepted. The first is a `packages/spec` test the claim's "their tests" covers (a typed member must delete its ledger line or that pin goes red, which the dev's `--project local` run showed). The second is the `os validate` door's pin for the very refusal this PR adds, test-only (+26/-0), in the file PR #23331 established for the rows' `onSuccess` door; it is the pin the card's "Wanted" implies for the author-facing surface, the dev stopped and explained it in the report, and the single-writer-path guard on the head is green. No source outside the surface was touched.

3. **Out of scope 1 (class b): the rows carry none of `ActionSchema`'s other `operation: 'update'` refusals** (`patch` without `operation`, `target` beside update, a non-`script` executor beside update, update with nothing to write, `list_toolbar` beside update each parse on a row and are refused by `ActionSchema`). Escalated, not fixed here — right. The card asks for one answer on the `onSuccess` pairing; these are the same family on other keys and the dev names a fold-in target ("the family's closing card") with dedupe words. **For the adopting seat / triage:** this finding has a static repro and no carrier card yet; a report comment is not a carrier (PR #23331's review said the same of its own escalation, which became this card). Route it to the family's closing card or file it.

4. **Out of scope 2: the new entry's sentence "A page's `properties` is not parsed on the metadata save or load path"** is true at this head and follows its three siblings' current wording, but PR #23418 rewrites that sentence in the siblings. Carrier named: whichever of #23418 / #23425 lands later aligns this entry. Answered: correct at this head, no action in this PR; the adopting seat should note the follow-up on #23418 if this lands first.

5. **hotcrm NOT MEASURED** (no checkout in the dev's container). Escalated as a residual: the card itself records that no producer was measured, the entry's `replacement` is a by-hand rewrite, and `os validate` reports the refusal at the row's `operation` / `onSuccess` so a hotcrm row carrying either shape is found at its next validate rather than silently dropped. Not a blocker for a `minor` pre-GA narrowing with a D3 entry; the adopting seat may measure hotcrm `0f84c9c` separately if it wants a zero rather than an unknown.

6. **`component.zod.ts:6030` ("a stored page still saves and loads") left as is** per the PM pointer, since #23418 owns that text. Answered: right, outside this diff.

7. **Check-runs in progress (18, named above).** Not a dev flag, but the one open input: the pins, typecheck, docs build and migration-registry test for this head are theirs to confirm. This verdict is on the contract; the merge waits on them by branch protection.
